questions.q: What positive effect of social media does lesson 1 describe?
a: People write far more and have become better at it
People read fewer books but remember them better
People speak more clearly in face-to-face talks
People spend less time typing than earlier generations
questions.why: Lesson 1 says we write more than any generation before and that character limits sharpen expression.

questions.q: Why does Pixar place its bathrooms in a central atrium?
a: To spark unplanned conversations that lead to new ideas
To save money on plumbing and building materials
To keep employees from taking long breaks
To make the campus easier for visitors to navigate
questions.why: Lesson 2 uses Pixar to show how chance encounters help combine unrelated ideas.

questions.q: Why does the summary advise keeping more casual online connections?
a: Acquaintances help spread and combine ideas in useful ways
Close friends are usually unwilling to share new ideas
Large follower counts directly increase your income
Casual contacts are less likely to disagree with you
questions.why: Lesson 2 says weak ties are especially good at spreading and mixing ideas.

questions.q: What did Facebook data show about couples with mutual friends?
a: They were more likely to stay together
They were more likely to argue in public
They had no measurable difference from other couples
They were less likely to share their social circles
questions.why: Lesson 2 reports that shared connections made couples less likely to lead separate lives.

questions.q: What is the online disinhibition effect?
a: People act cruelly when they believe there are no consequences
People become more honest when their names are visible
People write more carefully when strangers are watching
People avoid conflict in anonymous online spaces
questions.why: Lesson 3 says anonymity makes people feel free to let out their nastiness.
